fixes: Fix 1, reliability (apps/worker/src/worker.ts): attempt() wrote the job heap line in a finally block that could throw. A logger or sink that threw would fail a completed job, so pg-boss would run it again, or replace a failed job's own error. The line now sits in a try/catch that swallows the error. The weekly run still fails closed on a measured job with no heap line. The new worker.test.ts test, 'never lets the heap line change how an attempt ends', failed before the fix ('promise rejected synthetic sink failure') and passes after it.

Fix 2, the weekly heap check (tools/release-capacity/checks.ts): it held a job's live heap to 75% of V8's heap_size_limit. That limit is 752 MiB under the 560 MiB flag because it includes the young generation, so the line was 564 MiB where the alarm and the design use 420 MiB. The new heapLimitMib(command, logged) takes the smaller of the worker command's --max-old-space-size and the logged limit. checks.test.ts gained cases at 752 and with no flag. They failed first (1 failed of 21) and now pass (38 of 38 in tools/release-capacity). ADR 0083 and the ci.md runbook paragraph are updated, and the Revisit item is closed.

Fix 3, performance (apps/worker/src/triage/execute.ts, the candidates' query): NOT EXISTS (case_line) became NOT coalesce((SELECT true FROM case_line cl WHERE cl.service_line_id = p.service_line_id), false). The planner runs this per row through case_line_once, so there is no anti-join plan left to go wrong. The rows and their order are the same, because case_line_once allows one case line per line. Failing first: the gate's head runs of CAS-42.1 failed at 460 and 481 s. My diagnostic used the same database shape (100,000 lines, A and Y priced, autovacuum off, the cursor read as the worker's login). The old form was stopped at 120 s with 16,000 of 41,665 rows read; the new form read them all in 4.4 s. After the fix, CAS-42.1's report took 95.8 s against its 180 s budget.
